pinterest.title: All-Inclusive Greece Wedding Packages: What They Really Include
pinterest.description: Searching Greece wedding packages all inclusive? Here is the catch: at a Greek venue, all inclusive usually describes the holiday stay, not the wedding. Most packages bundle the ceremony set-up, a coordinator, flowers for the couple, a cake and a toast. The reception menu, drinks, guest rooms and outside suppliers are often quoted separately. Our guide compares ten Greek venue packages by what each one includes.

pinterest.title: Greece Wedding Packages All Inclusive: What Sits Outside the Package
pinterest.description: A Greek wedding package covers what its list names. The reception is the largest piece that tends to sit outside, along with drinks, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers. Some venues set a room or night minimum before a package applies, and some require a wedding planner on top. Read the guide to see where ten Greek venue packages draw the line, and what to ask for in writing.

pinterest.title: How to Compare Two All-Inclusive Greece Wedding Quotes Like for Like
pinterest.description: Two Greece wedding quotes compare only when they describe the same wedding. Set the guest count, spaces, hours and nights first. Then ask each venue the same questions: every inclusion in writing, which parts move with your guest list, deposit and cancellation terms, exclusive use, music finish times, a weather plan, step-free access and the quote currency.

slides: Searching for an all-inclusive Greece wedding package? At most Greek venues, all inclusive describes the holiday, not the wedding.
What a Greek venue package usually covers: the date and ceremony set-up, a coordinator, flowers for the couple, a cake and a toast.
What it rarely covers: the reception menu and drinks, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers.
Rooms are often a requirement rather than an inclusion. Some venues set a room or night minimum before a package applies.
Some venues require a wedding planner on top of the venue, so a package does not always remove that cost.
Planning a small wedding or elopement? Canaves sells a package for the couple alone, and Euphoria Resort scales its options for small groups.
Comparing quotes? Use the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency, with every inclusion listed in writing.

instagram_carousel.caption:
At most Greek wedding venues, all inclusive describes the holiday stay, not the wedding.

Our new guide puts ten Greek venue packages side by side, from Crete and Kos to Santorini, Mykonos and Athens, by what each one includes.

Most packages cover the ceremony set-up, a coordinator, flowers for the couple, a cake and a toast. The reception, drinks, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers are where they part ways, and most venues quote them separately.

A few things to ask every venue:
Which parts of the quote are fixed, and which move with your guest list?
Is there a room or night minimum?
Is the space yours alone, and for how many hours?
What time does the music stop?
Where does the celebration move if the weather turns?
Is a wedding planner required on top of the venue?

Prefer full control of your suppliers? Some venues, like the Myconian Collection, will prepare the stage for your own team.

Holding quotes that don't line up? Send us a message and a Wedded Advisor will talk them through with you. Full guide at the link in our bio.
